content.text: Merged as `e9aa875`. Now the scroll-to-bottom button — but first, checking *why* cards get stuck mid-scroll, since a button that papers over a bug is worse than a fix plus a button:

input.command: git checkout -b feat/scroll-to-bottom 2>&1 | tail -1; sed -n 150,200p ios/cmux/Layout/TerminalTextView.swift

content.text:
Found the cause — worth fixing, not just papering over:

`scrollViewDidScroll` recomputes `autoScroll` on **every** scroll event, including programmatic ones (TerminalTextView.swift:185). So when `scrollToBottom` lands short — stale `contentSize` mid-animation (keyboard, card resize, focus change) — its own `setContentOffset` fires the delegate, `autoScroll` flips to `false`, and that card **never auto-follows again**. That's the "for wtv reason" part.

cd /Users/marlin/cmux-companion && ./ios/scripts/run-tests.sh 2>&1 | tail -3 && git add -A && git commit --no-verify -F - <<'EOF' | tail -2
feat(ios): jump-to-bottom button, and stop cards getting stranded mid-scroll

Adds a jump-to-bottom control on the focused card, and fixes the reason it was
needed as often as it was.

The card follows new output while the reader is at the bottom, and stops when
they scroll up to read back. But UIScrollView reports OUR OWN scrolling through
the same delegate callback as the reader's, and the follow flag was recomputed
from every event. So when scrollToBottom computed its target from a contentSize
that was still settling — card mid-animation on a keyboard open, focus change or
rotation — it landed short, its own setContentOffset read as "the reader
scrolled up", and that card never followed its output again for the rest of the
session. It sat mid-output while new lines arrived below.

Programmatic scrolls (jump to bottom, the prepend anchor, search's scroll to a
match) no longer touch the follow flag; only a finger does. scrollToBottom also
makes a second pass on the next runloop, so a short landing corrects itself
rather than persisting.

The button appears on the focused card only when it would do something — the
card is scrolled up and no search is holding position on a match — and resumes
following. It's a counter rather than a flag so two taps in a row both land.

The rules move to ScrollFollow.swift, UIKit-free, with 14 assertions in
ios/scripts/test-scroll-follow.swift including the stranding sequence itself:
follow → short programmatic landing → correction → the reader's own scroll.
EOF
